capturedBy: Five headless `claude -p` turns driven from this worktree, into a session id created for
this capture and used for nothing else, so no line of this file comes from any real
conversation:
1. 'Reply with exactly the word: ok'          -> a user record with String content, and
an assistant text block.
2. 'Run this exact shell command with the      -> a tool_use / tool_result pair, the
Bash tool and then say done: echo hi'         result's content a plain String.
3. 'Think about this step by step before       -> a REDACTED thinking block (thinking
answering, then reply with just the           empty, signature present), which the
number: what is 17 times 3?'                  mapper must drop.
4. 'Read the file /tmp/t3-tiny.png with the    -> a tool_result whose content is a BLOCK
Read tool, then say: seen'                    ARRAY holding an image block, i.e. a
megabyte-class payload in the shape the
mapper must not carry.
5. 'Read the file /tmp/t3-tiny.pdf with the    -> a 'document' block in a user record,
Read tool, then say: read'                    another base64 payload, and a second
tool_result with String content.
/tmp/t3-tiny.png (8x8, 95 bytes) and /tmp/t3-tiny.pdf (605 bytes) were generated for the
capture so the payloads in this file are small and are nobody's data. They are inputs to
the capture, not part of it.
Source transcript:
~/.claude/projects/-Users-nate-Projects-Protos-n-Tools-flight-deck--claude-worktrees-fleet-pairing/
The plan's recipe used an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. That config dir carries no
credentials, so `claude -p` under it answers 'Not logged in - Please run /login' and
writes no transcript at all. The isolation it was buying - that nothing of a real
conversation can be captured - is instead bought by the session being a throwaway one
whose only five prompts are the ones quoted above.
editingRule: Lines may be DROPPED, never EDITED. This file is the source transcript filtered to drop
its six 'attachment' records; every surviving line is byte-for-byte what claude wrote.
The sha256 above is of this file as committed, and TimelineFixtureTests asserts it, so a
semantic edit that still parses as JSON is caught rather than only a truncation.
The six dropped lines are the SessionStart hook output, the agent listing and the skill
listing for this machine - the operator's private tooling setup, and nothing this
vocabulary maps. 'attachment' therefore has no captured example here; it is covered by a
hand-written line in ClaudeTimelineMapperTests instead, and dropping was chosen over the
alternative of editing one down to a publishable shape, which the rule forbids.
Still uncaptured, and hand-written in ClaudeTimelineMapperTests: an UNREDACTED thinking
block; an 'image' block in a user message (a paste); a tool_result whose content array
holds a TEXT element rather than an image; isCompactSummary and isSidechain records. No
scripted -p session produces any of them.
Also uncaptured, though the record IS here: the 'document' block arm. Claude marks the
PDF-attachment record isMeta, so the mapper drops it before any block is examined.
No schema for this format exists - the record shapes were established empirically (see
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-session-name-sync-design.md section 2 for the same
method applied to 'custom-title'). That makes this the same weak ground truth the codex
captures are: it records what claude DID on one day, not what it DECLARES.
Every fixture in Fixtures/ MUST be named *.captured.* to signal that it is verbatim
captured output, not authored. Tests reference captures by their documented name; if a
test cannot find its fixture, correct the lookup name in the test, never add an
undocumented copy under another name.
